agent_trace.summary: Hilar lymphadenopathy on a chest X-ray refers to enlargement of the hilar lymph nodes, which may appear as bilateral or unilateral hilar fullness or lobulated enlargement near the central mediastinum. On plain radiography, it can be subtle and may overlap with normal hilar vessels; the retrieved similar chest X-ray cases show the expected yes/no format for thoracic findings, but they do not specifically confirm hilar disease.

key_facts: The hila contain pulmonary arteries, veins, bronchi, and lymph nodes, so assessment on X-ray requires comparison of both sides.
Bilateral symmetric hilar enlargement can suggest lymphadenopathy, while vascular prominence can mimic it.
Chest X-ray is less sensitive than CT for detecting and characterizing hilar lymphadenopathy.
Associated mediastinal widening or paratracheal fullness can support an abnormal hilar/mediastinal process.
